newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields encouraged to lower close by currency.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields encouraged to lower close by currency.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.68 (PREV 92.57) 90-DAYS 7.23 (PREV 7.30)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.00 PCT (PREV 7.00) US 5-YR 6.72 (PREV 6.74)
* NZ bank bills close 7-8 points lower on currency strength
* Long bonds fall five points, offshore buying
* 90-day bills seen making assault on 7.0 pct within weeks
New Zealand yields closed lower across the curve following steady trading on Monday and traders see further downside, particularly in the front end.
"The general feeling is that 7.0 percent is the next level. I think we will see 7.0 percent in the next couple of weeks," said a Wellington bill dealer.
The 90-day yields closed at 7.23 percent from Friday's 7.30 percent, backed by another muscular performance by the New Zealand dollar.
Dealers said all eyes these days are on the Monetary Conditions Index and as the Trade-Weighted Index causes that to rise, yields fall.

Last week's encouraging inflation, retail sales and current account data was still feeding into the market. Traders reported good offshore buying interest in the bond market overnight, particularly in the shorter-dated maturities.
As well, strong selling of long bonds from an Auckland bank evident through much of last week appeared to have dried up.
One dealer said that if selling from that source died then the curve would have a chance to flatten and the long bonds would fall further.
The June bank bill futures closed up nine points at 92.68 on volume of 3672.
Bancorp said liquidity continues to slosh around in the overnight market, giving corporates a very cheap source of working capital funding.
With call at 7.00 percent and 90-days at 7.24 percent, Bancorp sees very low risk in accessing this funding for borrowers.
